title: data/now.json
description: What I am listening to and reading, for the homepage's Now strip and literature.html's Reading Now. The track is written weekly by .github/scripts/refresh_now.py from Last.fm (recent tracks), keeping its previous value when the fetch fails; the books in progress come from my Goodreads library export, written by .github/scripts/refresh_books.py --export through refresh_now.write_reading(), and a weekly run keeps them as they are.

track.description: The most recent Last.fm scrobble, or null when Last.fm has none and there was no previous one to keep.

url.description: The track's Last.fm page; the Now strip links to it, falling back to music.html when empty.

nowPlaying.description: True when Last.fm reported it as playing at fetch time. Only this makes the strip's equaliser bounce (.is-playing); with a weekly refresh it is almost always false.

reading.description: Books on the currently-reading shelf of my last Goodreads export, at most three, in the export's order (the most recently touched first). The Now strip shows the first and a count of the rest.

title.description: Title as the export gives it, series in brackets, curly quotes straightened.

link.description: My Goodreads review page for the book (review/show/<id>) when the shelf knows it, else the book's page (book/show/<id>).

img.description: The book's cover as a path on this site: the small copy (240px tall) of it beside the shelf's covers (refresh_books.reading_cover: the shelf's own copy, or Open Library's cover fetched once). Absent when there is none; never an address on another site, so Reading Now asks no other site for a picture.

updated.description: Date of the weekly refresh that wrote the track, YYYY-MM-DD.

readingUpdated.description: The day the Goodreads export the books in progress came from was downloaded, YYYY-MM-DD. Reading Now dates its list by it (js/bookshelf.js), so a list from an old export shows its age.
